topic: Testing and contracts: pytest, property tests, OpenAPI contract tests
why: An FDE ships an API into a customer's environment and then leaves; the customer's integration team keeps building against it for years, and the only thing that protects them from your successor's refactor is a machine-checked contract that fails the build. Customer data is the adversary: unicode task names, empty lists, 10 MB payloads, and out-of-order state transitions arrive on day one of production, and property-based tests are the cheapest way to meet them in CI first. A published coverage number and a green contract job are also what a customer's procurement and security review actually ask for in the vendor questionnaire, so the test suite is part of the sales artefact, not just engineering hygiene.
prerequisites: Production Python architecture (topic 25): the Kaupex Task Compiler's domain/repository split, Protocol-typed ports and the KaupexError hierarchy (InvalidTransition, NotFound, Conflict) that tests will assert on
FastAPI in production (topic 26): Depends, dependency_overrides, lifespan, settings via pydantic-settings, and the problem+json error handlers
PostgreSQL at depth (topic 29): SQLAlchemy 2.0 async engine and sessions, Alembic migrations, transactions and SAVEPOINT semantics
Docker running locally (topics 5-6) so testcontainers can start a Postgres container; understands ports, volumes and image tags
CI/CD (topic 18): can read and edit a GitHub Actions workflow with jobs, services, artifacts and required status checks
JSON Schema vocabulary as emitted by pydantic v2: type, required, properties, additionalProperties, enum, format, minLength/maxLength, anyOf

subtopics.name: Test layers for a FastAPI + Postgres + Temporal service
subtopics.learn: Lay out tests/unit (pure domain, no IO, milliseconds), tests/integration (repositories against a real Postgres), tests/api (handlers through the ASGI app) and tests/contract (Schemathesis against the OpenAPI document), each behind a registered marker so `pytest -m unit` runs in under five seconds and the full suite runs in CI. Use the src layout with `--import-mode=importlib` so test files need no `__init__.py` and can share basenames, set `testpaths = ["tests"]`, and put shared fixtures in a root conftest.py with layer-specific conftest.py files below it. Decide what each layer is allowed to touch: unit tests may not import sqlalchemy or httpx; integration tests may not mock the database; API tests may override dependencies but not monkeypatch internals. Be able to argue why a bug should be caught at a given layer and why moving a test down a layer makes it faster and more precise.

resource.label: pytest docs - Good Integration Practices (test layout, src layout, import modes)

subtopics.name: pytest configuration as a hard gate
subtopics.learn: Configure `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` so the suite fails on anything ambiguous: `addopts = "-ra --strict-markers --strict-config --import-mode=importlib"`, `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]` with narrow `ignore::DeprecationWarning:third_party.*` exceptions, `xfail_strict = true` so an xfail that starts passing fails the build, `faulthandler_timeout = 60`, `minversion`, `required_plugins` and `markers = [...]` for every custom marker. Know the debugging flags cold: `-x`/`--maxfail=3`, `--lf`, `--ff`, `--sw` (stepwise), `--pdb`, `-k "transition and not cancel"`, `--durations=10 --durations-min=0.5`, `--co -q` to check collection, `-p no:randomly` to pin ordering. Know the exit codes: 0 all passed, 1 failures, 2 interrupted, 3 internal error, 4 usage error, 5 no tests collected; a `-k` expression matching nothing returns 5 and must not be treated as success by a wrapper script.

resource.label: pytest docs - API Reference (ini options and command-line flags)

subtopics.name: Fixtures: scope, teardown order, conftest layering, factories
subtopics.learn: Understand fixture scopes (function, class, module, package, session), that a higher-scoped fixture cannot request a lower-scoped one (ScopeMismatch), and that yield fixtures tear down in reverse dependency order, so a session-scoped Postgres container outlives the function-scoped session that borrows a connection from it. Use `request.addfinalizer` when teardown must run even if setup partially failed, `autouse=True` only for cross-cutting invariants (reset `app.dependency_overrides`, clear a Redis test DB), and fixture overriding in a nested conftest.py to swap a real adapter for a fake in one directory. Prefer factory fixtures (`make_task(**overrides)` returning a domain object with sane defaults) over dozens of near-identical fixtures; inspect what is active with `pytest --fixtures`, `--fixtures-per-test` and `--setup-show`. Know that `tmp_path`, `monkeypatch` and `caplog` are function-scoped and that `tmp_path_factory` is the session-scoped alternative.

resource.label: pytest docs - How to use fixtures

subtopics.name: Parametrize as a state-transition matrix
subtopics.learn: Encode the Kaupex Task state machine as a table: `@pytest.mark.parametrize("state,event,expected", CASES, ids=...)` where CASES covers every (state, event) pair and `expected` is either the next state or `InvalidTransition`, so the test file is the executable specification of allowed transitions. Use `pytest.param(..., marks=pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="..."))` for known gaps instead of deleting rows, stack two parametrize decorators for a cartesian product, `indirect=True` to route a parameter through a fixture (build the task in the requested state against the real DB), and `pytest_generate_tests` when the matrix must be computed from the enum at collection time so a new state cannot be added without a test row. Readable ids (`ids=lambda c: f"{c.state}-{c.event}"`) make `-k "queued-cancel"` selection and CI failure output usable.

resource.label: pytest docs - How to parametrize fixtures and test functions

subtopics.name: Test doubles at the boundary: monkeypatch, autospec, respx, in-memory fakes
subtopics.learn: Use `monkeypatch.setattr/setenv/delenv/setitem/chdir` for process-level state and `unittest.mock.patch("kaupex.adapters.llm.AsyncAnthropic", autospec=True)` with `spec_set=True` so a renamed or misspelled method raises AttributeError instead of silently returning a Mock; use `AsyncMock` for coroutines and `assert_awaited_once_with`. Patch where the name is looked up (the importing module), not where it is defined. For HTTP boundaries prefer `respx.mock` routers (`respx.post(url).mock(return_value=httpx.Response(429, headers={"retry-after": "1"}))`, `assert_all_called=True`) so retry and backoff paths are exercised against realistic responses. For the persistence boundary prefer an in-memory fake that implements the same `TaskRepository` Protocol, run the same test module against both fake and real repository (parametrised fixture), and never mock a SQLAlchemy Session: the mock will pass while the query is wrong.

resource.label: Python docs - unittest.mock (patch, autospec, spec_set, AsyncMock)

subtopics.name: Async API tests through ASGITransport with dependency overrides
subtopics.learn: Configure pytest-asyncio with `asyncio_mode = "auto"` and `asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session"` so a session-scoped async engine and the test share one event loop; otherwise asyncpg raises 'attached to a different loop' on the second test. Build the client as `httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=app), base_url="http://test")`; know that ASGITransport does not run lifespan, so wrap with `asgi_lifespan.LifespanManager(app)` when startup wiring (pool creation, Temporal client) matters. Override `get_session` and `get_current_user` via `app.dependency_overrides[...]` inside a fixture and call `app.dependency_overrides.clear()` in teardown; keep one test that uses a real signed JWT so the auth path is not permanently bypassed. Assert status code, full JSON body, `content-type: application/problem+json` on errors and the `X-Request-ID` header, and rely on server exceptions propagating into the test rather than being turned into a 500 you then miss.

resource.label: FastAPI docs - Async Tests (httpx ASGITransport)

subtopics.name: Real Postgres in tests: testcontainers, migrations, rollback isolation, xdist
subtopics.learn: Start `PostgresContainer("postgres:16-alpine")` once per session, take `get_connection_url()`, and run `alembic.command.upgrade(cfg, "head")` against it so every CI run also proves the migration chain applies from empty. Isolate tests with the SQLAlchemy 'join an external transaction' recipe: open a connection, `begin()`, bind the session, `begin_nested()` for a SAVEPOINT, roll back at teardown; fall back to `TRUNCATE ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE` for tests that must observe a real commit (advisory locks, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` workers). For RLS-protected tables (topic 30) the test session must `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id` exactly as the app does or every query returns zero rows. Under pytest-xdist derive the database from `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` (`kaupex_test_gw0`) with `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE kaupex_test` so workers never share rows, and know the CI fallbacks when Docker is unavailable: a GitHub Actions `services:` container or `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true` in restricted runners.

resource.label: testcontainers-python docs - Postgres module

subtopics.name: Property-based testing with Hypothesis: strategies, shrinking, properties worth writing
subtopics.learn: Write `@given(st.text(), st.integers(min_value=0))` tests and understand that Hypothesis searches then shrinks to a minimal counterexample, which is why a failure reads like `text=''` rather than a 300-character string. Build strategies for domain types with `st.builds(TaskCreate, name=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=120))`, `st.from_type(...)` for simple pydantic models (constrained fields need explicit strategies), `st.sampled_from(TaskState)`, `st.lists(..., unique_by=...)`, `st.one_of`, `.map/.filter/.flatmap`, `@st.composite`, `assume()` for cheap preconditions and `@example(...)` to pin past regressions. Know the property families and pick the right one: round-trip (`Task.model_validate_json(t.model_dump_json()) == t`), invariant (compiled task DAG is acyclic), idempotence (normalise twice equals once), oracle (naive implementation equals optimised), and metamorphic (adding a step never shortens the plan). Read health checks (`too_slow`, `filter_too_much`, `data_too_large`) as strategy bugs to fix, not warnings to suppress.

resource.label: Hypothesis docs - Quick start guide

subtopics.name: Deterministic Hypothesis in CI: settings profiles, example database, reproduce_failure
subtopics.learn: Register profiles in conftest.py: `settings.register_profile("ci", max_examples=500, deadline=None, derandomize=True, print_blob=True)` and `"dev"` with `max_examples=50`, then `settings.load_profile(os.getenv("HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE", "dev"))`; select with `--hypothesis-profile` and pin with `--hypothesis-seed`. Understand the `.hypothesis/examples` DirectoryBasedExampleDatabase (gitignored, cached between CI runs with actions/cache or replaced by `GitHubArtifactDatabase` so a failure found on main is replayed on every branch), and paste the `@reproduce_failure(version, blob)` line from a `print_blob=True` report into the test to pin a specific counterexample. Know that the 200 ms default `deadline` is flaky on loaded CI runners and why `deadline=None` is the honest fix, and that a Hypothesis `Flaky` error means the test failed then passed on replay: the code under test is nondeterministic (time, dict order, uncontrolled randomness), not the framework.

resource.label: Hypothesis docs - API reference (settings, database, reproduce_failure)

subtopics.name: Stateful testing of the Task lifecycle with RuleBasedStateMachine
subtopics.learn: Model the Task service as a `RuleBasedStateMachine`: `tasks = Bundle("tasks")`, `@initialize()` to create a tenant, `@rule(target=tasks, payload=st.builds(...))` that calls create and returns the id, `@rule(task=tasks, event=st.sampled_from(Event))` that applies a transition and mirrors it in a plain-dict model, `consumes(tasks)` on delete, `@precondition(lambda self: self.model)` to gate rules, and `@invariant()` that after every step asserts each real task equals the model and every terminal task has `completed_at` set. Export with `TestTaskMachine = TaskMachine.TestCase` and `TestTaskMachine.settings = settings(max_examples=200, stateful_step_count=30)`. When it fails, Hypothesis prints the minimal `state.create(...)`, `state.transition(...)` sequence; paste it into a regression test. This is how you find the cancel-after-complete and double-retry bugs that a parametrised matrix cannot express because they depend on history.

resource.label: Hypothesis docs - Stateful testing

subtopics.name: OpenAPI as the contract: making FastAPI's generated schema complete and strict
subtopics.learn: Every route must declare what it can actually return: `response_model=`, `status_code=201`, and `responses={404: {"model": Problem}, 409: {"model": Problem}, 422: {"model": Problem}}` with `content` keyed by `application/problem+json`, otherwise Schemathesis `status_code_conformance` and `content_type_conformance` fail on the first real error. Set stable operation ids with `generate_unique_id_function=lambda r: f"{r.tags[0]}_{r.name}"` (or `operation_id=`) because generated clients and OpenAPI links key on them. Make request models `ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` so the schema emits `additionalProperties: false` and `negative_data_rejection` has teeth; push `Field(min_length, max_length, pattern, ge, le)` constraints into the schema so generated data hits real boundaries; document response headers under `responses[200]["headers"]`; hide `/healthz` and `/readyz` with `include_in_schema=False`; use `openapi_extra` for anything FastAPI cannot express, such as `links`.

resource.label: FastAPI docs - Additional Responses in OpenAPI

subtopics.name: Committed schema snapshot and breaking-change detection with oasdiff
subtopics.learn: Commit `openapi.json` and add a test `assert app.openapi() == json.loads(Path("openapi.json").read_text())` with a `make openapi` target to regenerate, so any schema change appears as a reviewable diff in the PR rather than a surprise to the customer's client generator. In CI fetch the base with `git show origin/main:openapi.json > base.json` and run `oasdiff breaking base.json openapi.json --fail-on ERR`; know the classes it flags: removed path or method, new required request property, removed or renamed response property, type narrowing, enum value removed from a request or added to a response, `required` added to a response schema, and know which of those are ERR versus WARN and why an added optional response field is not breaking. Use `oasdiff changelog` output as the PR comment and the customer-facing release note. Define the policy: a breaking diff requires a `/v2` path or a major version bump plus a deprecation window, and the CI job enforces it rather than a reviewer's memory.

resource.label: oasdiff - OpenAPI diff and breaking-change detection (GitHub)

subtopics.name: Schemathesis CLI: phases, checks, and reading a failure
subtopics.learn: Run `schemathesis run http://127.0.0.1:8000/openapi.json --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --max-examples 100 --seed 42 --max-failures 10 --wait-for-schema 30 --report junit` (or a file schema plus `--url`) and understand the four phases: examples (schema `example`/`examples` values), coverage (boundary values, `maxLength+1`, missing required fields, wrong types), fuzzing (Hypothesis-generated data) and stateful (OpenAPI links). Know each default check and what a failure means for Kaupex: `not_a_server_error` (unhandled exception), `status_code_conformance` (undocumented 403), `content_type_conformance`, `response_headers_conformance`, `response_schema_conformance` (nullable field not marked), `negative_data_rejection` (invalid body accepted), `positive_data_acceptance` (valid body rejected), `missing_required_header`, `unsupported_method`, `use_after_free`, `ensure_resource_availability`, `ignored_auth` (endpoint answers without a token). Tune with `--exclude-checks`, `--include-path-regex '^/v1/tasks'`, `--max-response-time 1.5`, `--phases`, and `schemathesis.toml` sections such as `[checks.negative_data_rejection] expected-statuses = ["400", "422"]`; reproduce a failure from the printed curl command and `--report-vcr-path`.

resource.label: Schemathesis docs - Checks reference

subtopics.name: Schemathesis inside pytest: from_asgi, parametrize, OpenAPI links, stateful
subtopics.learn: Load the schema straight from the app with `schema = schemathesis.openapi.from_asgi("/openapi.json", app)`, or from a fixture via `schemathesis.pytest.from_fixture("api_schema")` so the app under test carries the same `dependency_overrides` (test DB, fixed clock) as the rest of the suite; write `@schema.parametrize() def test_api(case): case.call_and_validate(headers=auth)` and scope with `schema.include(operation_id=...)` / `schema.exclude(path_regex=...)`. Add explicit `links` under `responses.201` via `openapi_extra` (`"operationId": "tasks_get_task", "parameters": {"task_id": "$response.body#/id"}`) so `APIWorkflow = schema.as_state_machine(); TestAPI = APIWorkflow.TestCase` chains create, get, transition and delete and `use_after_free` catches a GET 200 after DELETE. Retrofit conformance onto existing handwritten API tests with `schema["/v1/tasks/{task_id}"]["GET"].validate_response(response)`. Mark all of this `@pytest.mark.contract` and run it as its own CI job because it is minutes, not seconds.

resource.label: Schemathesis docs - Testing Python Apps (from_asgi, from_fixture)

subtopics.name: Coverage that measures the truth: branch, greenlet concurrency, exclusions, fail_under
subtopics.learn: Configure `[tool.coverage.run]` with `source = ["kaupex"]`, `branch = true`, `parallel = true`, `relative_files = true` and `concurrency = ["thread", "greenlet"]`: SQLAlchemy's asyncio bridge runs DB calls inside greenlets and without the greenlet tracer the lines inside repositories report as never executed. In `[tool.coverage.report]` set `fail_under = 85`, `show_missing = true`, `skip_covered = true`, and `exclude_also` for `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, `raise NotImplementedError`, `@abstractmethod` and the `__main__` guard; `omit` generated migrations. Drive it through pytest-cov (`--cov=kaupex --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=85`) and use `--cov-context=test` to see which test covers which line when deciding what to delete. Know the difference between line and branch percentages, why an `except` clause with no test is a branch miss, and why the number is a floor for finding untested modules (`coverage report --sort=miss`) rather than a quality score.

resource.label: coverage.py docs - Configuration reference

subtopics.name: Subprocess and worker coverage: parallel data files and combine
subtopics.learn: Code that runs in a child process is invisible to coverage by default: a Temporal worker started with `subprocess.Popen`, a CLI invoked in an integration test, or a `multiprocessing` pool. Enable measurement either with `patch = ["subprocess"]` in `[tool.coverage.run]` (coverage 7.10+) or the older `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START=pyproject.toml` environment variable plus the `.pth` hook, set `sigterm = true` so a worker killed by SIGTERM still flushes its `.coverage.<host>.<pid>.<random>` data file, and add `multiprocessing` to `concurrency` when pools are involved. After the run, `coverage combine` merges the data files, then `coverage report` and `coverage xml -o coverage.xml`; pytest-cov does the combine automatically for xdist workers but not for your own subprocesses. When unit and integration run in separate CI jobs, upload the `.coverage.*` files as artifacts and combine in a final job, which only works with `relative_files = true` because the checkout paths differ.

resource.label: coverage.py docs - Measuring sub-processes

subtopics.name: CI wiring: unit, integration and contract jobs that block merge
subtopics.learn: Split the workflow into a `unit` job (`pytest -m "not integration and not contract" -n auto`), an `integration` job with `services: postgres: image: postgres:16` plus `options: --health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 10s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 5` and `ports: ["5432:5432"]`, and a `contract` job that starts `uvicorn kaupex.main:app --port 8000 &` then runs `schemathesis run http://127.0.0.1:8000/openapi.json --wait-for-schema 30 --report junit --max-examples 50 --seed ${{ github.run_id }}` and uploads `schemathesis-report/` with actions/upload-artifact (or uses `schemathesis/action@v3`). Add the `oasdiff breaking` step, `--junitxml` for the test summary, `actions/cache` on `.hypothesis`, `timeout-minutes` on every job and `concurrency: group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true`. Then make it a gate: branch protection with all three jobs as required status checks, so 'a failing contract breaks the build' is enforced by the repository, not by the reviewer noticing a red check.

resource.label: GitHub Docs - Creating PostgreSQL service containers

subtopics.name: Publishing coverage: Codecov upload, patch gates, and the badge
subtopics.learn: Upload `coverage.xml` with `codecov/codecov-action@v5` (`files: coverage.xml`, `fail_ci_if_error: true`, `token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}`), then write a `codecov.yml` where `coverage.status.project.default.target: auto` with `threshold: 1%` stops regressions and `coverage.status.patch.default.target: 80%` is the gate that actually matters on a PR: new code must be tested even when the repo total is low. Embed the badge markdown from the Codecov settings page in the README so the number is public and updates itself. Know the SaaS-free alternative for a customer's air-gapped repo: `coverage json` and `jq .totals.percent_covered` produce a shields endpoint JSON (`{"schemaVersion": 1, "label": "coverage", "message": "87%", "color": "green"}`) committed to a gh-pages branch or gist and rendered via `img.shields.io/endpoint?url=...`, and publish `htmlcov/` as a build artifact so a reviewer can open the missed lines.

resource.label: Codecov docs - Status badges

subtopics.name: Flaky tests: ordering, clocks, timeouts and quarantine policy
subtopics.learn: Install pytest-randomly so every run shuffles test order and reseeds `random`, Faker and NumPy; when a failure appears, reproduce with the printed `--randomly-seed=N` and disable with `-p no:randomly` only to bisect, never in CI. Add pytest-timeout (`timeout = 120` in ini, `--timeout-method=thread` when signals are unavailable) so a hung Temporal client fails the job in two minutes instead of six hours. Control time with time-machine (`time_machine.travel(...)`) rather than `sleep()`, and replace sleeps in async tests with a poll-until-deadline helper. Know the five root causes to check in order: shared mutable state across tests, clock, network, ordering, event loop or connection reused across loops. Define a quarantine policy: a `@pytest.mark.flaky` marker excluded from the required job, a ticket with owner and expiry, and `pytest-repeat --count=50` to prove a fix; never put pytest-rerunfailures on the required check because it converts a real race into green.

resource.label: pytest-randomly - official repository (README)

subtopics.name: Mutation testing and assertion quality: why coverage lies
subtopics.learn: Configure `[tool.mutmut] paths_to_mutate = ["src/kaupex/domain/"]` and `tests_dir = ["tests/unit/"]`, run `mutmut run`, then `mutmut results` and `mutmut show <id>` (or `mutmut browse`) to read surviving mutants: a flipped `<` to `<=` or a removed `raise` that no test noticed. Every survivor is a line that is covered but not asserted, which is how a 92% covered module still ships a wrong transition guard. Fix survivors by strengthening assertions, not adding tests: `pytest.raises(InvalidTransition, match=r"queued -> done")` instead of bare `pytest.raises(Exception)`, exact `response.json() == {...}` instead of `"id" in response.json()`, `pytest.approx` with explicit tolerance, and `assert result` never on its own. Run mutation testing on the domain package only and on a schedule or on demand, not as a required gate, because a full run is minutes to hours.

resource.label: mutmut docs - mutation testing for Python

outcomes: You can run `pytest -m unit` on the Kaupex Task Compiler in under five seconds and the full suite (unit, integration against a testcontainers Postgres, API, contract) in CI, with `--strict-markers --strict-config`, `filterwarnings = error` and `xfail_strict = true` enforced and every marker registered.

You can write a Hypothesis `RuleBasedStateMachine` for the Task lifecycle that, when a deliberately planted bug allows cancel after complete, prints a minimal three-step counterexample which you turn into a pinned regression test with `@reproduce_failure` or `@example`.

You can make a full `schemathesis run` against the Kaupex `/openapi.json` pass with all default checks enabled and at least one OpenAPI link exercised in the stateful phase, and explain from the failure output which handler or schema field was wrong for any check you had to fix along the way.

You can demonstrate that adding a required property to a request model or deleting a response field fails the `oasdiff breaking --fail-on ERR` job and the committed `openapi.json` snapshot test, while adding an optional response field passes both.

You can show branch coverage for the async repository layer moving from near zero to accurate by adding `concurrency = ["thread", "greenlet"]`, and explain why the pre-fix number was wrong rather than low.

You can configure a Postgres-backed test suite to run under `pytest -n auto` with one database per xdist worker derived from `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER`, with zero cross-worker failures across ten consecutive runs.

You can set up branch protection so a PR cannot merge while any of unit, integration, contract or oasdiff jobs is red, and a Codecov patch status below 80% is visible on the PR with the badge in the README reflecting main.
You can run `mutmut` on `kaupex/domain`, pick three surviving mutants and kill each by tightening an assertion rather than adding a test, explaining what the original assertion failed to check.
failureModes: A route returns 409 from the `Conflict` handler but only 200 and 422 are declared in `responses=`; the customer's generated TypeScript client treats 409 as an unknown error and retries the task creation in a loop, producing duplicate tasks until Schemathesis `status_code_conformance` is finally added to CI three months later.

Repository tests run against a mocked SQLAlchemy Session that returns whatever the test says; the real query has a missing `tenant_id` predicate, tests are green, and the first cross-tenant data exposure is found by the customer's security team during UAT.

Coverage is 91% and celebrated, but `concurrency` was never set so every line inside the greenlet-bridged async repository counts as executed only when the sync fallback path runs; after a refactor the badge stays green while the actual async code path has no test.

The API suite shares a module-scoped async engine with function-scoped tests under pytest-asyncio's default function loop; the second test fails with 'Future attached to a different loop', the team adds `pytest-rerunfailures`, and a genuine connection-pool leak hides behind retries for months.

`openapi.json` is regenerated on every deploy but never committed or diffed; a pydantic model rename changes `status` to `state` in the response, no test fails because the app and its own schema still agree, and the customer's integration breaks on Monday morning.

Hypothesis runs with the default 200 ms `deadline` on shared CI runners; property tests fail intermittently under load, someone adds `suppress_health_check` and `@settings(max_examples=5)` to make CI green, and the tests stop finding anything.

Integration tests `TRUNCATE` tables between runs but xdist workers share one database; tests pass locally with `-p no:xdist` and fail randomly in CI, so the team drops parallelism and the suite grows to a 40-minute serial run that nobody waits for before merging.
interviewQuestions: A customer's integration team says our API 'changed under them' although every deploy passed CI. Walk me through what a contract-testing setup that would have caught it looks like, what specifically runs in CI, what counts as a breaking change, and how you would roll the change out instead.

Design the test strategy for a FastAPI service backed by Postgres with row-level security and Temporal workers. What runs at each layer, what is real versus faked, how do you isolate tests that must commit, and how do you keep the whole thing under ten minutes in CI with parallel workers?

You have 90% line coverage and a production bug in a state-transition guard that every test exercised. Explain why coverage did not catch it, what mutation testing would have shown, and how you would decide which assertions to strengthen.

Schemathesis reports `response_schema_conformance` failures on GET /v1/tasks/{id} for about 2% of generated cases and `ignored_auth` on one endpoint. Debug both: what are the likely causes in a pydantic/FastAPI app, how do you reproduce one case, and which fix belongs in the schema versus the handler?

Write a property-based test for the Kaupex task compiler that would find an ordering bug the parametrised unit tests cannot. What property do you state, what strategy generates the inputs, how do you keep it deterministic in CI, and what do you do when Hypothesis reports Flaky?

A customer's security questionnaire asks for our test coverage and how we prevent regressions in the API they consume. What do you send them, how is it produced, and what claim would you refuse to make from a coverage number alone?
